items.title: Design the Android sitemap, adaptive shell and navigation behavior
items.outcome: Android has an approved compact, medium and expanded navigation model, route inventory and shell states before android#1 or any feature screen is implemented.
items.context: The primary personal surface contains debt, transactions, planning and trust. A phone-only bottom bar or copied web sitemap would break tablets, Back behavior and feature discovery.
scope: Compact navigation bar and top app bar
Expanded rail/drawer and list-detail patterns
Launch, lock, update, maintenance, home and deep-link landing
Predictive Back, edge-to-edge, IME, process-death and task restoration
Route, parent, title, primary action and analytics IDs
acceptance_criteria: Every Android registry screen has one route and parent or documented system/deep-link entry
Primary compact destinations stay within Material guidance and every remaining feature is reachable through tested IA
Expanded layouts are structural adaptations and never duplicate financial state across panes
System Back and predictive Back are specified for every top-level, nested and overlay destination
android#1 and T-AND-07 receive D6 shell and window-class handoffs
contracts_schema: Route and shell state IDs reference T-UXR-05 allocation and T-UX-01 states
security_privacy: Account switch and privacy lock remove prior-user data from all panes
Deep links reveal no protected content before authentication and authorization
observability: Navigation first-click, backtrack, deep-link recovery and orphan-route signals without financial content
tests: Predictive-Back and protected deep-link specification review
rollout_rollback: D6 shell handoff precedes android#1 Ready
Route changes preserve old deep links through a versioned migration table
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and Android shell page. The Android Design Lead owns route templates; feature squads instantiate them without editing shared navigation.
definition_of_done: All routes and shell states registered
IA and platform tests pass
Android, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android authentication, onboarding, consent, permissions and recovery
items.outcome: Users can register, recover, understand consent and choose every optional permission without coercion, while a deny-everything user still reaches manual value.
items.context: Permission trust and recovery abuse determine adoption and security. These journeys must be tested as prototypes before Android implementation or Play declaration evidence.
scope: Register, verify, sign in, sign out everywhere and passkey
Lost-device recovery, code, reverification, cooling-off, cancel and reenrollment
Purpose consent, age eligibility and permission dashboard
SMS and notification rationale, deny, do-not-ask, restricted settings, revoke and recover
Manual/privacy-first activation and synthetic first transaction
acceptance_criteria: A participant who denies every permission completes onboarding and records a manual transaction
Consent and permission screens distinguish purpose, scope, optionality, withdrawal and consequence
Recovery cancellation is reachable from a non-enrolled device and restricted actions during cooling-off are visible
SMS and notification access use separate rationale and recovery paths with no coaching or confirm-shaming
T-AND-01, T-AUTH-02, T-CMP-02, android#9 and android#10 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps T-AUTH-01, T-CON-09, T-CON-11 and platform permission states to screens and content
security_privacy: No screen exposes account existence, recovery secret or raw notification/message content
Permission denial remains private and does not reduce unrelated functionality
observability: Comprehension, denial, recovery cancel, restricted-settings return and manual activation without content
rollout_rollback: D6 and T-RES-02 findings precede mapped implementation Ready
A permission flow can remain disabled while manual onboarding stays complete
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Identity, consent and permission subflows use separate owned sections and one shared security/content review.
definition_of_done: All auth/onboarding/permission screens and states registered
Moderated, accessibility and abuse evidence accepted
Security, Compliance, Content and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android home, debt list, detail and debt-free status
items.outcome: The Android home and core debt surfaces make payoff status, attention, data freshness and derivation understandable without shame, false certainty or hidden assumptions.
items.context: Debt-free status is the primary retention hook and first proof of value. It needs OnTrack, NotOnTrack, empty, stale and partial states before visual momentum is trusted.
scope: Home debt-free countdown and attention queue
Debt list, basic add/edit, detail, archive and restore
OnTrack, NotOnTrack/never-payoff, incomplete, stale and offline
Debt progress, schedule summary, provenance and derivation
Largest-text, TalkBack and compact/expanded variants
acceptance_criteria: Participants correctly explain the payoff date or why no payoff date exists
Home never presents stale, partial or projected data as confirmed current status
Debt add/edit states show units, validation and ledger-safe archive consequence
Every chart/progress treatment has a complete text alternative
android#2 and android#3 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-01 debt and tagged projection states plus freshness and derivation fields
security_privacy: Privacy mode masks amounts and recents without hiding status/recovery
Synthetic debt examples avoid lender endorsements
observability: Payoff comprehension, derivation open, empty activation and stale recovery without amounts
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes android#2/#3 Ready
Momentum visuals can be disabled while textual status remains
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Home and debt-detail branches share approved debt components and converge in the Android platform prototype.
definition_of_done: Home/debt screens and states registered
Comprehension and accessibility evidence accepted
Money-path, Content and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android strategies, simulator and advanced debt scenarios
items.outcome: Android users compare strategies and advanced credit-card, prepayment and refinance scenarios as neutral, understandable options with complete derivation and accessible controls.
items.context: Small-screen comparisons can bias a strategy through placement and hide assumptions behind a slider. The product must explain deterministic outcomes without advising.
scope: Avalanche, snowball, hybrid and custom comparison
Extra-payment, lump-sum and target-date simulator
Credit-card cycle and minimum-payment trap
Prepayment/refinance break-even and utilization-first scenarios
Derivation, disclaimers, stale/incomplete and no-solution states
acceptance_criteria: Strategies have equal visual weight before selection and order bias is tested
Slider/inputs expose exact value, bounds and keyboard/switch alternatives and debounce state
Minimum-payment trap and scenario charts include table/text alternatives
Refinance and salary implications remain scenarios, never instructions or guarantees
android#4 and T-DEBT-04 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-01 strategy, simulation, advanced debt and refusal/error variants
security_privacy: No lender/product recommendation or creditworthiness judgment
No client-side recomputation in design requirements
observability: Strategy comprehension, scenario correction, derivation use and abandoned no-solution state without values
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped implementation Ready
Advanced scenarios remain gated without altering basic debt flow
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Comparison, simulator and advanced-scenario sections can be designed in parallel over one neutral-option pattern.
definition_of_done: All strategy/scenario screens and states registered
Bias, comprehension and accessibility tests pass
Compliance, Money-path and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android transactions, accounts, categories and statement import
items.outcome: Manual entry, account/category management, transaction review/reversal and statement import are fast, precise, offline-safe and understandable on compact and expanded Android layouts.
items.context: Manual/privacy-first users depend on these surfaces, and imported or edited data can create lasting ledger effects. Preview, conflict and reversal must be designed before forms.
scope: Manual transaction, account and category create/edit/archive/merge
Timeline, search/filter, detail, edit and reversal
File picker, mapping, dry-run preview, duplicate/conflict review, commit and result
Cash/refund reconciliation entry points
Offline queue, validation, process-death and partial failure
acceptance_criteria: Manual entry completes with every optional permission denied and supports amount/date/category corrections
Reversal is visually distinct from deletion and states the ledger effect
Import writes nothing before preview and repeat import explains duplicate safety
Long lists meet paging, TalkBack, focus and constrained-memory specifications
T-AND-02, T-AND-03, T-AND-04 and T-AND-05 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps transaction, T-CON-10 import, T-CON-17 query and ledger error fields
security_privacy: File previews remain local until explicit commit and contain no analytics content
Privacy mask and shared-device behavior cover lists and recents
observability: Manual completion, validation correction, reversal undo and import preview/commit without values
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped implementation Ready
Import can remain disabled while manual and read-only flows remain
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Manual/timeline and import sections use separate branches over shared transaction components.
definition_of_done: All transaction/account/import screens and states registered
Usability, offline and accessibility evidence accepted
Money-path and Android approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android capture health, clarification, email and receipt review
items.outcome: Users understand capture health and can resolve SMS, notification, email or receipt candidates without exposing raw content or allowing uncertain data to become a transaction silently.
items.context: Capture is useful only when failures are visible and correction is cheap. Email/receipt permission and image states add separate trust and review needs.
scope: Capture-health dashboard and revoked/paused states
Batched clarification list, candidate comparison and rule preview/rollback
Notification/SMS duplicate/conflict and already-resolved states
Mailbox connect/revoke and on-device processing disclosure
Receipt camera/framing/OCR review/edit/confirm and image-retention choice
acceptance_criteria: Every source shows active, paused, denied, revoked, degraded and last-success state without raw content
Clarification displays structured provenance and why a candidate won, never message text
Rule creation/rollback shows affected scope and concurrent resolution
Receipt creates no transaction until editable review is explicitly confirmed and default image retention is off
android#11, android#12, T-ING-01 and T-ING-02 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-02, T-CON-15, capture-health, rule, email and receipt candidate states
security_privacy: No raw message/email or retained receipt image in artifacts, telemetry or server flows
Source permission scope and revocation are explicit
observability: Capture-health view, clarification resolution, rule rollback and receipt correction without content
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped frontend Ready
Each capture source can remain disabled and manual entry remains complete
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Capture health, clarification, email and receipt subflows use separate sections and one privacy review.
definition_of_done: All capture/review screens and states registered
Privacy, comprehension and accessibility evidence accepted
Security and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android income, budgets, recurring items and bill calendar
items.outcome: Fixed and irregular income, category budgets, safe-to-spend, bills, recurring charges and sinking funds form one understandable planning experience with derivation and timing uncertainty.
items.context: Salary awareness is a core request and late/variable income changes every budget message. Reminders cannot leak amounts and safe-to-spend cannot look guaranteed.
scope: Income source/setup/history and irregular schedule
Budget list/category detail/rollover and safe-to-spend derivation
Bill calendar and reminder settings
Recurring-charge review/cancel tracking
Sinking-fund create/contribute/progress and late/short income states
acceptance_criteria: Safe-to-spend shows derivation, data age and incomplete-income warning
Late or short salary never appears as user failure and offers a feasible recovery path
Bill/reminder notification designs carry no monetary value
Budget, recurring and sinking-fund states work offline and at largest text scale
T-INC-03 and related Android reporting receive a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps income, budget, recurring, bill and sinking-fund contract states and derivations
security_privacy: Notification pointers reveal no amounts or merchant
Income content is masked in privacy/shared-device modes
observability: Setup completion, derivation open, rollover confusion and recurring review without values
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-INC-03 Ready
Individual planning modules can remain gated without changing ledger data
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Income/budget and recurring/calendar branches share planning components and converge in the platform prototype.
definition_of_done: All income/budget/recurring screens and states registered
Comprehension and accessibility tests pass
Content and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android goals, net worth, holdings and financial reports
items.outcome: Goals, net worth, holdings and reports show progress, tradeoffs, provenance, per-currency separation and uncertainty without instructions or hidden conversion.
items.context: The founder requested car, home and debt-free goals plus salary implications. Small-screen summaries must preserve derivation and advice boundaries.
scope: Goal list/create/detail/progress/contribution
Goal competition and scenario comparison
Salary-market range/source/age
Net-worth per-currency overview/trend/drill-down
Holding create/revalue/archive/composition and category/period reports
acceptance_criteria: Goal tradeoffs are presented as user-selected options and never a job/investment instruction
Salary-market data shows source, age, range and limitation
Net worth never combines currencies without approved conversion
Holding staleness and partial portfolios cannot appear current or complete
T-GOL-02, T-NWT-02, T-NWT-05 and T-AND-05 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-08 goals, income provenance, holdings, freshness, completeness and derivation
security_privacy: No employability or creditworthiness score
Privacy mode masks sensitive amounts and report previews
observability: Goal comprehension, tradeoff selection, stale revaluation and report task without amounts
rollout_rollback: D6 mappings precede implementation Ready
Salary or advanced holdings panels remain disabled if evidence expires
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Goal and net-worth/holding/report branches use shared data components and separate compliance review.
definition_of_done: All goal/net-worth/report screens and states registered
Comprehension, accessibility and advice tests pass
Compliance, Money-path and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design the Android split-group lifecycle and settlement experience
items.outcome: Organizers, members and non-users can enter itemized expenses, understand exact shares, dispute and settle through a transparent non-custodial Android flow.
items.context: Split virality depends on low-friction invites, but money correctness and dispute visibility cannot be sacrificed for conversion.
scope: Group create/list/detail/archive
Member and placeholder invite/claim
Expense and itemized bill entry
Equal/exact/percentage/share allocation and remainder derivation
Simplify, settle via external deep link, dispute, resolution and export
acceptance_criteria: The UI refuses a split that does not reconcile and shows the deterministic remainder
Every member can inspect how their share derives from items and rules
Placeholder claim and payment deep links reveal no private group data before verification
Dispute state and resolution are visible to every authorized member
T-SPL-02 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-04 split, allocation, settlement, dispute and simplification states
security_privacy: No contact inventory or payment credential access
External payment handoff is clearly non-custodial
observability: Invite, split correction, derivation open, dispute and settlement completion without amounts/relationships
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-SPL-02 Ready
Simplification can remain gated while original obligations remain authoritative
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Invite, expense and settlement/dispute sections use separate branches over shared split components.
definition_of_done: All split screens and states registered
Reconciliation, privacy and accessibility evidence accepted
Money-path and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android family sharing, household goals and safe exit
items.outcome: Household members can grant, inspect, revoke, leave and contribute to authorized aggregates/goals while Android remains safe under coercion, shared-device and offline-cache conditions.
items.context: Family finance can become surveillance. Aggregate/detail grants, revocation bounds, access logs and discreet exit must be visible and independently abuse-tested.
scope: Invite/accept/decline and eligibility
Per-person/category aggregate and detail grants
Access log and shared-data visibility
Household partial/suppressed dashboard and joint goals
Revoke, cached-data expiry, discreet exit, duress concealment and neutral notifications
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate is default and detail requires a separate explicit grant with consequence
Aggregate-only users see no detail affordance and partial/suppressed never appears zero
Revocation states both online and offline bounds and clears cached content on schedule
Exit requires no reason, avoids dramatic notification and remains reachable with assistive technology
T-FAM-03, T-FAM-06, T-TRU-04 and T-TRU-05 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-04 grant, access event, aggregate completeness/suppression, contribution and revocation states
security_privacy: Independent coercive-control and differencing review required
No paired household participant recruitment or implicit whole-household grant
observability: Grant escalation, access-log view, revoke/exit and suppression without identities, relationships or amounts
tests: Offline lease/cache eviction and accessibility review
rollout_rollback: D6 and abuse evidence precede sharing Ready
Feature remains disabled when safety evidence or contract version expires
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Grant, household and safe-exit sections have separate owners but one Security/Inclusive Design approval.
definition_of_done: All family/household screens and states registered
Abuse, privacy, accessibility and comprehension evidence accepted
Security, Inclusive Design and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android assistant, BYOK, history and natural-language drafts
items.outcome: Android assistant surfaces expose model status, citations, derivation, refusal, draft confirmation, history and provider configuration safely on constrained screens.
items.context: A conversational surface can obscure provenance and destructive effects. The interface must remain subordinate to deterministic actions and protect secrets/recovery.
scope: Assistant entry, answer, citations, derivation and refusal
Contest/override and deterministic fallback
Natural-language transaction draft/correct/cancel/expire/confirm
History off/opt-in/list/export/delete
BYOK/custom endpoint add/replace/revoke/pending/suspend and quota
acceptance_criteria: Every answer is disclosed as model output with current disclaimer and provenance
Draft writes nothing until all fields are visible and explicit confirmation succeeds idempotently
No screen/error/notification exposes a provider key or client-direct endpoint path
Recovery suspension and cooling-off/cancellation are complete and understandable
T-AIP-03 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-14, T-CON-16, quota, provider, refusal and history states
security_privacy: No prompt/answer content in analytics or artifact examples
Backend-only provider routing and least-disclosing notifications
observability: Refusal, citation, draft and key lifecycle outcomes without content
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-AIP-03 Ready
Assistant/config modules can be independently disabled
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Answer, draft/history and provider-settings sections are separate branches over one assistant trust pattern.
definition_of_done: All assistant screens/states registered
Security, compliance and accessibility evidence accepted
Content and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android billing, notification preferences and retention messaging
items.outcome: Purchase, restore, cancel, grace, quota, notification choices and retention messages are transparent, reversible and free of dark patterns or leaked amounts.
items.context: Billing and notification flows intersect platform policy and user trust. Cancellation, deferred purchase and immutable security messages require explicit native states.
scope: Plan/current entitlement/quota
Purchase pending/deferred/success/failure and restore
Grace/hold/cancel/renewal disclosure
Notification class/channel/quiet hours and immutable security messages
Milestone/digest/dormancy content and in-app fallback
acceptance_criteria: Cancel is no harder to find or complete than subscribe and no control is preselected deceptively
Client never grants entitlement before server verification and pending/deferred are distinct
Notification copy and payload design contain no monetary value or sensitive content
A user with notifications denied can access the same product messages in-app
T-BIL-03, T-NOT-02, T-NOT-04 and T-RET-01 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps billing lifecycle/version/quota and T-CON-11 notification preference/delivery states
security_privacy: No payment credential collection
Security notifications cannot be disabled and carry pointer-only payloads
observability: Purchase/restore/cancel and preference task outcomes without amounts
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped implementation Ready
Promotional/retention messages can be disabled without hiding account state
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Billing and preferences/retention sections are separate branches sharing status and disclosure components.
definition_of_done: All billing/notification states registered
Dark-pattern, recovery and accessibility tests pass
Compliance, Content and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android trust, privacy, support and account control
items.outcome: Android users can lock/conceal the app, inspect consent/access, export/correct/delete data and obtain support through truthful, accessible and recoverable controls.
items.context: Trust features are the operational proof of privacy. Deletion and support need progress, limits and failure rather than an instant-success message.
scope: App lock, timeout, privacy mode, recents and screen protection
Consent, analytics opt-out and transparency
Export, correction, deletion and rights request status
Support create/list/detail/thread and diagnostic preview
Step-up, partial failure, verified completion and safe retry
acceptance_criteria: Privacy/lock states protect recents and shared-device use without blocking safe recovery
Consent withdrawal shows consequence and preserves unrelated functionality
Export/deletion show step-up, progress, residue/partial failure and verified completion
Diagnostic preview lists included fields and rejects raw messages, secrets and amounts
T-TRU-01, T-TRU-02 and T-SUP-02 receive exact D6 mappings
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-09 and T-CON-11 consent, rights, transparency, support and deletion states
security_privacy: Least-disclosing defaults and neutral safe-exit content
No operator identity or hidden resource leaks
observability: Trust task success, support discovery, export/delete completion and diagnostic rejection without content
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped implementation Ready
If fulfillment is unavailable, intake/progress fails honestly and escalates
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Privacy, rights and support sections have separate owners and one Compliance/Security review.
definition_of_done: All trust/support screens and states registered
Privacy, accessibility and comprehension evidence accepted
Compliance, Security and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design Android constrained-device, offline and adaptive failure behavior
items.outcome: Every core Android journey remains understandable and recoverable under low memory/storage, low bandwidth, process death, force stop, restricted settings, large screens and accessibility settings.
items.context: India-first Android behavior cannot be approved only on a flagship emulator. Resource and OEM behavior changes what users can capture, sync and recover.
scope: Compact/medium/expanded and multi-window variants
Low memory/storage and ten-thousand-row paging
Offline queue, stale, conflict, poison item and sync recovery
Force-stop/private-space/restricted-settings and tracking paused
Largest text, TalkBack, switch access, high contrast and reduced motion
acceptance_criteria: Core journeys have registered variants for every T-QA-12 device/profile class
No resource failure loses a queued financial mutation or presents pending as confirmed
Expanded panes never leak a prior account or duplicate authoritative state
Tracking-paused and restricted-setting recovery explain limits and manual alternatives
T-AND-06 and T-QA-08 receive complete design evidence
contracts_schema: Maps platform capability, resource-degraded, capture-health and sync states without a private taxonomy
security_privacy: Fallbacks never weaken encryption, privacy masking or permission scope
Debug/queue inspection is absent from release design
observability: Profile-specific overflow, recovery, tracking-paused and accessibility task outcomes
rollout_rollback: Design evidence precedes T-AND-06/T-QA-08 closure
Affected optional feature disables rather than lowering platform/security baseline
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Adaptive and failure-state specialists annotate platform flow branches without changing product hierarchy.
definition_of_done: All device/failure variants registered
Device and assistive-tech evidence accepted
Android, Accessibility, QA and CDO approvals recorded
D6 evidence published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design the debt-progress Android home-screen widget and privacy states
items.outcome: A deliberately optional debt-progress home-screen widget can reinforce the core goal without exposing balances, debt identity or unsafe data on a locked/shared launcher.
items.context: The countdown is the retention hook, but a launcher widget is a privacy surface. The feature was previously omitted rather than explicitly designed or declined.
scope: Glance widget sizes and configuration
Privacy-safe progress modes with amount hidden by default
Locked, stale, no-data, setup, update and tap/deep-link states
Refresh/battery behavior and accessibility
Product decision to ship, defer or decline with evidence
acceptance_criteria: Default widget reveals no balance, debt name, merchant, salary or household data
Locked/shared-device and screenshot review shows only user-approved information
Stale/projection status remains visible without implying current certainty
Widget tap authenticates before protected detail and works with TalkBack
The ship/defer/decline decision and implementation consequence for T-AND-08 are recorded
contracts_schema: Widget consumes privacy-safe debt status and freshness identifiers; no new financial calculation
security_privacy: Opt-in, least disclosure and immediate disable/delete
No sensitive push or launcher cache content
observability: Opt-in, configuration, stale state and authenticated deep-link outcome without financial values
rollout_rollback: Feature remains disabled until privacy review and user evidence support it
Rollback removes widget updates and clears cached presentation
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Widget design is isolated from the app home flow and can be declined without blocking the Android platform gate.
